## Portable integration provenance

This export preserves the accepted producer's scientific text, with two documented status-only sentence changes reflecting completed independent review and this integration. The original producer JSON remains exact inside the structured companion. The earlier HMB-only proposal used the 279-assessment checkpoint `ccf7ff8ed64485bd7867c46a2d7c9f5e0426b57f` and added no identity; the combined HMB/krill update refines this existing calcium-HMB decision and adds one separate krill-preparation assessment, bringing the ledger to 280. The earlier Kyowa trial, its gait-positive result and its calcium-free control remain separate from this TSI bed-rest preparation. Producer, independent-source reviewer and integrating-reviewer reading scopes remain separately attributed. Exporting these documents adds no primary-reading or biological-replication credit. Raw sources and native assets remain outside Git. Original correspondence bodies, historical registry versions and the locked protocol/SAP remain unavailable. scientific_summary: Separately, the recovered original main and official supplement for PMID 23514626 test TSI calcium-HMB sachets during ten-day bed rest and eight-week rehabilitation after five-day pretreatment in healthy older adults. Twenty-four were randomized (11 control/13 active); bed-rest evaluable counts were 8/11, and full-study counts 7/11. The all-evaluable total lean-mass change contrast was nonsignificant (P=.16); excluding one active male with suspected, unproven baseline DXA error yielded nominal total/leg mass contrasts P=.02 (8/10), while the same-cohort female subgroup was 7/8 with total-mass P=.04. These are population-specific sensitivity findings, not strength benefit. Actual strength and functional tests were performed; printed knee-extension bed-rest treatment P values were .84 and .10, and the main reported no end-bed-rest SPPB, Get-Up-and-Go or five-item treatment differences. Within-arm recovery improvements and missing individual estimates do not establish treatment benefit, equivalence or universal ineffectiveness. The current NCT00945581 record lists strength as primary and mass/function/activity as secondary; historical versions/SAP and the registry 36-versus-paper 24 enrollment discrepancy remain unresolved. The nominally shared maltodextrin/calcium background differs from the earlier Kyowa trial control; exact elemental-calcium matching and product interchangeability remain unverified. Two SAEs, one per arm, were judged unrelated by the authors; no safety-equivalence claim follows. Continued supplementation during rehabilitation is not off-treatment durability. Preserve the earlier separate-trial gait positive and its control/access limits. This source adds no BUBR1 restoration, productive renewal, fidelity or MVA efficacy; source reporting conflicts and unread comment/reply bodies remain explicit.
